plain: Would you like to secretly make someone's vote count against the side they back tomorrow?
dinniman: Picture it: they raise their hand, full of conviction, and every bit of that support quietly subtracts itself. No fingerprints. Would you like to secretly make someone's vote count against the side they back tomorrow?

plain: Do you fancy pinching a person's vote overnight so it works backwards for them?
dinniman: Wasn't me. Wasn't anybody. Somebody's vote just happens to point the wrong way now, and that's a coincidence I'm not going to investigate. Do you fancy pinching a person's vote overnight so it works backwards for them?

plain: Would you like to change how much another player's vote is worth?
dinniman: One person, one vote is SUCH a peasant idea. Some votes deserve to count more, some deserve to count against, and I should decide which. Would you like to change how much another player's vote is worth?

plain: Would you like to hand someone a vote that counts three times over tomorrow?
dinniman: Form 3B, the Ballot Amplification Request, signed in triplicate. Approved! Sponsors adore a landslide. Would you like to hand someone a vote that counts three times over tomorrow?

plain: Do you enjoy using official paperwork to give one chosen person a lot more say at the vote?
dinniman: Seen this a hundred times. Some clerk with a stamp decides one idiot's hand is worth three, and the whole floor dies because of it. Do you enjoy using official paperwork to give one chosen person a lot more say at the vote?

plain: Would you like to make someone else's ability work twice in one night?
dinniman: Double espresso, darling, but for powers! One sip and their little trick fires TWICE. Would you like to make someone else's ability work twice in one night?

plain: Would you like to make sure one player is sober, healthy and told only the truth for a night?
dinniman: Everybody down here is drunk, poisoned or lied to, usually all three. Sometimes the kindest thing is one clear cup for one person. Would you like to make sure one player is sober, healthy and told only the truth for a night?

plain: Would you like to give another player a short boost to their own ability, lasting until the next dusk?
dinniman: Limited-time power-up! Expires at dusk! Non-refundable! Side effects include hope! Would you like to give another player a short boost to their own ability, lasting until the next dusk?

plain: Would you invite someone to share their secret identity with you, knowing it might kill you both?
dinniman: Come sit, sweetheart. Tell me who you really are. Of course, there's a small chance we both end up dead, but isn't honesty worth it? Would you invite someone to share their secret identity with you, knowing it might kill you both?

plain: Do you only want to learn someone's character if they agree to tell you?
dinniman: I'm not prying it out of anyone with a crowbar. If they say yes, great. If they say no, I'll live, which honestly is more than the other option guarantees. Do you only want to learn someone's character if they agree to tell you?

plain: Once someone has been executed today, would you like to be allowed to nominate again?
dinniman: The crowd has had its hanging and everyone's heading home, and you stand up and say 'more please'. The ratings! Once someone has been executed today, would you like to be allowed to nominate again?

plain: Would you like the power to hold a second trial on a day that has already had its execution?
dinniman: ONE EXECUTION?! What is this, a petting zoo? Bring me another one! Would you like the power to hold a second trial on a day that has already had its execution?

plain: Would you like to point at one player and have somebody else's character change that night?
dinniman: You press the big red button marked 'them' and the zap lands on someone completely different. That's not a bug, that's science. Would you like to point at one player and have somebody else's character change that night?

plain: Do you enjoy daily experiments that turn a player other than your target into a new character?
dinniman: Wire alpha to wire beta, buzzer off, stand very still, and BEHOLD! The wrong person has transformed, as planned. Do you enjoy daily experiments that turn a player other than your target into a new character?

plain: Would you like to shoot someone dead just because of how they voted?
dinniman: The first tally's in. You saw who raised a hand. You've got a six-shooter and an attitude. Would you like to shoot someone dead just because of how they voted?

plain: Do you watch the day's first vote closely, ready to punish someone who took part in it?
dinniman: New achievement unlocked: Quick Draw! Awarded for ending a voter's career right after the count. Reward: one dented spittoon. Do you watch the day's first vote closely, ready to punish someone who took part in it?

plain: Would you like to rearrange where people sit around the circle?
dinniman: Master Carl, you will sit THERE. Lady Katia, beside the window. No, I don't care that you were comfortable. Would you like to rearrange where people sit around the circle?

plain: Would you forbid players from leaving their seats to talk in private?
dinniman: No sneaking off to the corridor. No little huddles by the snack table. If you've got something to say, say it where everyone can hear. Would you forbid players from leaving their seats to talk in private?

plain: Would you like to kill one of your neighbours, but only if your other neighbour agrees?
dinniman: Nice shoes on the fella to your left. Shame if something happened to him. All you need is a nod from the fella on your right. Would you like to kill one of your neighbours, but only if your other neighbour agrees?

plain: Do you prefer your daytime murders arranged with the blessing of the person sitting beside you?
dinniman: Here's how it works on this floor: no hit goes down without a handshake from the guy next to you. Honour among killers. Do you prefer your daytime murders arranged with the blessing of the person sitting beside you?

plain: Would you like to let a dead player use their ability again for a while, without bringing them back to life?
dinniman: They're still dead, mind you. Very dead. But for one short stretch their old trick works again, which is creepy and also useful. Would you like to let a dead player use their ability again for a while, without bringing them back to life?

plain: Would you save one grisly favour for the whole game, briefly reviving a corpse's power?
dinniman: Hair, teeth, fragments of poems, a dead man's talent on loan until sundown. One per customer! Would you save one grisly favour for the whole game, briefly reviving a corpse's power?

plain: Would you like a once-per-game power to decide yourself whether a nominated execution passes or fails, whatever the vote says?
dinniman: ORDER! The court has heard enough of your pathetic hand-waving. I alone decide if this one swings or walks! Would you like a once-per-game power to decide yourself whether a nominated execution passes or fails, whatever the vote says?

plain: Would you like to rule a vote a failure, so nobody is executed at all, even after enough people voted?
dinniman: The mob has done its counting, the rope is ready, and you get to say case dismissed, nobody hangs today. Would you like to rule a vote a failure, so nobody is executed at all, even after enough people voted?

plain: After seeing a vote, would you like the power to declare the execution anyway, however few hands went up?
dinniman: Democracy is lovely, darling, until it gets in your way. Then it is merely a suggestion. After seeing a vote, would you like the power to declare the execution anyway, however few hands went up?

plain: Would you like to pick up a trade on your first night that depends on your side: a Townsfolk skill if good, a Minion trick if evil?
dinniman: Welcome, apprentice! Your starter class is randomised based on your moral compass. Good kids get hammers. Bad kids get knives. Would you like to pick up a trade on your first night that depends on your side: a Townsfolk skill if good, a Minion trick if evil?

plain: As a newcomer, would you like to arrive with no ability of your own and be taught one on your first night?
dinniman: Everybody starts somewhere. Showing up with empty hands and learning the local craft overnight isn't weakness, it's how you grow. As a newcomer, would you like to arrive with no ability of your own and be taught one on your first night?

plain: Would you be content to vote only when someone hands you their vote token?
dinniman: Spare a token, guv? Bless you! Look at me, Carl, I'm an ACTOR. A tragic, starving actor who can only vote on charity. Would you be content to vote only when someone hands you their vote token?

plain: Would you like to learn a dead player's alignment when they give you something?
dinniman: Funny thing about charity. You learn a lot about a person from the fact that they gave it. Would you like to learn a dead player's alignment when they give you something?

plain: Would you like to be permanently sober and healthy, whatever anyone tries to do to you?
dinniman: Poison? Bounces off. Booze? Water to me, honey. I've been through worse than your little potions. Would you like to be permanently sober and healthy, whatever anyone tries to do to you?

plain: Do you think being funny enough should keep you from being exiled?
dinniman: Tough crowd tonight! But if they laugh, they can't throw you out. That's in the contract. Probably. Do you think being funny enough should keep you from being exiled?

plain: Would you rely on your sense of humour, rather than your innocence, to survive the town's judgement?
dinniman: Look, nobody believes I'm innocent. But I did get a laugh earlier with the bit about the goblin, and apparently that counts. Would you rely on your sense of humour, rather than your innocence, to survive the town's judgement?

plain: Would you take a teammate's place at the gallows if they were executed?
dinniman: Somebody on your team is about to swing. You step forward, smile, and say 'I'll take it from here'. Would you take a teammate's place at the gallows if they were executed?

plain: Would you happily be the one who gets blamed and hanged so an ally walks free?
dinniman: Friendly newcomer! Dandy attitude! Does not ask what the rope is for! Our sponsors call this an ideal brand ambassador. Would you happily be the one who gets blamed and hanged so an ally walks free?

plain: Would you like to kill anyone who dares nominate a particular teammate of yours?
dinniman: TOUCH MY FRIEND AND I WILL FEAST ON YOUR SPLEEN! Anyone who nominates them DIES! Would you like to kill anyone who dares nominate a particular teammate of yours?

plain: Would you like the whole town to start the game knowing a player who shares your alignment?
dinniman: Mongo! Mongo stomp! (Mongo means everyone already knows who his best friend is, and they'd better not lay a finger on them.) Would you like the whole town to start the game knowing a player who shares your alignment?

plain: Would you like to take nominations away from the players and leave them to the Storyteller alone?
dinniman: Hear ye! The faithful shall no longer point their grubby fingers. Only the Storyteller may name the accused! Would you like to take nominations away from the players and leave them to the Storyteller alone?

plain: Would you like to guarantee that at least one member of the opposing team is nominated every day?
dinniman: Here's a fun rule: every single day, the other side gets someone in the dock, no excuses. Would you like to guarantee that at least one member of the opposing team is nominated every day?

plain: Would you like a vote where only you and the dead get a say?
dinniman: The living have had their chance and blew it. From now on, it's you and the ghosts. Would you like a vote where only you and the dead get a say?

plain: Would you scrap the need for a majority, so even a handful of votes can carry an execution?
dinniman: Majority? Quorum? That's a lot of paperwork for one hanging. A few hands should do it. Would you scrap the need for a majority, so even a handful of votes can carry an execution?

plain: Would you like every dead player in town to have a stronger say at the vote than usual?
dinniman: Dead viewers are still viewers! Engagement is engagement! Let us put every ghost back on the ballot. Would you like every dead player in town to have a stronger say at the vote than usual?

plain: Would you like to protect new players by threatening whoever is most responsible for killing them?
dinniman: Hurt the new kid and the sky opens up. I've seen a lot of rules down here, and that's one of the few I actually like. Would you like to protect new players by threatening whoever is most responsible for killing them?

plain: Would you call down trouble on anyone who knocks a first-time player out of the game?
dinniman: BEHOLD my divine wrath! Strike down the innocent beginner and I shall rain fire upon your smug little head! Would you call down trouble on anyone who knocks a first-time player out of the game?

plain: Would you bend the rules so newcomers get protection or breathing room from the veterans?
dinniman: I remember being new and terrified. If the game can give beginners a little shelter from the people who've played a hundred times, I'm all for it. Would you bend the rules so newcomers get protection or breathing room from the veterans?

plain: Would you make experienced players stay quiet for the first couple of minutes of each day?
dinniman: Two minutes. That's all. The old hands sit on their hands, and the new folks get a word in before the know-it-alls take over. Would you make experienced players stay quiet for the first couple of minutes of each day?

plain: Do you believe veterans should hold their tongues each morning so beginners can speak first?
dinniman: New patch notes! Veteran crawlers now suffer a mandatory two-minute Mute debuff at the start of each day. Fresh meat may now speak. Do you believe veterans should hold their tongues each morning so beginners can speak first?

plain: Would you like rules that force some of the players to stay silent at certain moments?
dinniman: Silence, darlings, is the most DRAMATIC sound there is. Everyone hushed, every eye on the one person still allowed to speak. Would you like rules that force some of the players to stay silent at certain moments?

plain: Would you like the Storyteller to make a deliberate mistake, fix it and own up to it publicly?
dinniman: It's not a bug, it's a feature! And when it IS a bug, we announce it to the whole audience with a big apology banner. Brand transparency! Would you like the Storyteller to make a deliberate mistake, fix it and own up to it publicly?

plain: Do you find it endearing when the person running a game admits they got something wrong?
dinniman: Oh, I love it when the big boss goes red in the face and says 'whoops, my bad'. Makes my whole damn day. Do you find it endearing when the person running a game admits they got something wrong?

plain: Would you like a special rule, known to everyone, that smooths over an awkward clash between particular characters?
dinniman: When two abilities collide and nobody knows what happens, someone has to write it down and read it out loud. Would you like a special rule, known to everyone, that smooths over an awkward clash between particular characters?

plain: Do you enjoy announcing the official clause that explains exactly how two troublesome characters interact?
dinniman: Section nine, subsection 'these two hate each other'. Everybody listen, because I'm only explaining this once. Do you enjoy announcing the official clause that explains exactly how two troublesome characters interact?

plain: Would you give every player a once-per-game chance to doom someone on their own team?
dinniman: WOE! WOE UPON THE VILLAGE! Each of you may offer up one of your own to the void! I find this deeply moving! Would you give every player a once-per-game chance to doom someone on their own team?

plain: While four or more players live, would you let anyone publicly call for the death of someone on their own side?
dinniman: Folks, the doom-preacher is in the building, and tonight anyone can stand up and point at a teammate! The audience is losing its mind! While four or more players live, would you let anyone publicly call for the death of someone on their own side?

plain: Would you like to host a daily gathering where up to three guests learn how many of them are evil?
dinniman: Tea at six fifteen. Scones at six forty-five. Three guests, darling, and each one goes home knowing a little something about the others. Would you like to host a daily gathering where up to three guests learn how many of them are evil?

plain: Do you enjoy having visitors call on you, knowing one of them will leave with false gossip?
dinniman: My salon is EXCLUSIVE. Three visitors only. And one of them will leave whispering absolute nonsense, which is half the fun. Do you enjoy having visitors call on you, knowing one of them will leave with false gossip?

plain: Would you give every dead player one more vote on the final day?
dinniman: When the end comes, the ghosts get their tokens back for one last ride. Even dead crawlers get to vote on the finale. Would you give every dead player one more vote on the final day?

plain: Do you believe the dead should get their say back when the game reaches its very last day?
dinniman: FINALE NIGHT! Every corpse in the house gets a voice! The dead vote counts! Viewership up four hundred percent! Do you believe the dead should get their say back when the game reaches its very last day?

plain: Would you like to help the Storyteller give one good player a single piece of wrong information, just once all game?
dinniman: Tee-hee. Just one tiny lie, once, to one nice person. That's practically nothing. That's barely a prank. Would you like to help the Storyteller give one good player a single piece of wrong information, just once all game?

plain: Do you like the idea of one sneaky fib, somewhere in the game, keeping the good team from trusting everything?
dinniman: Stay humble, team. Somewhere in this game there might be one piece of info that's a giggling little lie, and nobody's to blame. Do you like the idea of one sneaky fib, somewhere in the game, keeping the good team from trusting everything?

plain: Would you like the game to come down to a head-to-head contest where everyone picks the winner?
dinniman: Two contestants. One stage. The whole crowd votes on who walks away a champion. This is what television was MADE for! Would you like the game to come down to a head-to-head contest where everyone picks the winner?

plain: Would you give the Demon one chance to challenge an opponent to a showdown that the whole town judges?
dinniman: BLOOD! GLORY! The Demon calls out a challenger and the mortals choose who wins! I would watch this every night! Would you give the Demon one chance to challenge an opponent to a showdown that the whole town judges?

plain: Would you like something bad to happen to anyone who talks when the Storyteller has asked for silence?
dinniman: Shhh. The Storyteller asked nicely. Talk now and something very large with very many teeth comes out of the stacks. Would you like something bad to happen to anyone who talks when the Storyteller has asked for silence?

plain: Are you the sort who wants people chattering through important announcements to face real consequences?
dinniman: Mongo... GRR. (Mongo has noticed you talking while the nice lady was explaining the rules, and Mongo would like you to stop or be eaten.) Are you the sort who wants people chattering through important announcements to face real consequences?

plain: Would you like the whole town to know that two particular neighbours are on the same side?
dinniman: Two seats, side by side, publicly declared comrades. Very touching. Very suspicious. Would you like the whole town to know that two particular neighbours are on the same side?

plain: Would you reveal a pair of allies to everyone, then let one of them register falsely just once?
dinniman: United we stand, until one of us shows up wrong on somebody's reading. One crack, that's all I'd allow. Would you reveal a pair of allies to everyone, then let one of them register falsely just once?

plain: As someone shaping the game rather than playing in it, would you like to let in one extra Outsider, or turn one away?
dinniman: Name, please. Papers, please. One more misfit through the gate, or one fewer. You decide, officer. As someone shaping the game rather than playing in it, would you like to let in one extra Outsider, or turn one away?

plain: Do you like standing guard at the town gate, deciding whether one more misfit gets in?
dinniman: Some people want adventure. Some people want a little booth, a stamp and the power to say 'not today'. Do you like standing guard at the town gate, deciding whether one more misfit gets in?

plain: Would you set a firm limit so that evil can never gain more than one extra player?
dinniman: Converts, recruits, turncoats, all very exciting, until there are nine of them and the show's over by lunch. Would you set a firm limit so that evil can never gain more than one extra player?

plain: As a rule-keeper, would you rather cap evil's recruiting than let converts pile up without limit?
dinniman: The great spirit watches. The great spirit counts. And the great spirit says ONE extra villain, no more, or I start screaming. As a rule-keeper, would you rather cap evil's recruiting than let converts pile up without limit?

plain: Would you make a standing rule that the Demon must voluntarily skip at least one attack during the game?
dinniman: It buzzes! It walks downstairs! It forces the monster to take a night off! Fun for all ages! Would you make a standing rule that the Demon must voluntarily skip at least one attack during the game?

plain: Would you like evil players to get their usual starting information even in a very small game?
dinniman: Tiny game, tiny crowd, still gets the deluxe evil starter pack. Every villain deserves their goodie bag! Would you like evil players to get their usual starting information even in a very small game?

plain: Would you make each nominee pick one defender who alone may speak until the vote?
dinniman: Every accused gets one lawyer, and everyone else shuts up until the hands go up. It's the only courtroom down here with any manners. Would you make each nominee pick one defender who alone may speak until the vote?

plain: Do you like forcing someone to argue a nominee's innocence, at the risk of their life if they don't?
dinniman: Tell us, sweetheart, in your own words, why they're innocent. Convincingly, please. Your life depends on it. Do you like forcing someone to argue a nominee's innocence, at the risk of their life if they don't?

plain: Do you love games full of homebrew characters and house rules?
dinniman: Unofficial content detected! Unlicensed abilities! Fan-made nonsense! The legal team is screaming and I have never been happier. Do you love games full of homebrew characters and house rules?

plain: Would you rather play a fan-made script than an official one?
dinniman: The official stuff's fine, I guess. But some guy's kitchen-table creation with a character called 'The Haberdasher of Doom'? Now you've got my attention. Would you rather play a fan-made script than an official one?

plain: Would you like the Storyteller to hand-pick every player's character instead of dealing them at random?
dinniman: Random draws are for COMMONERS. Every role should be placed with care, like a tiara on the right head. Would you like the Storyteller to hand-pick every player's character instead of dealing them at random?

plain: Do you prefer a carefully tended game, with every character planted on purpose rather than by luck?
dinniman: I always liked a garden where somebody actually thought about what goes where. Same with a game, honestly. Do you prefer a carefully tended game, with every character planted on purpose rather than by luck?

plain: Would you wear a silly hat, speak only one sound at a time and vote twice for the privilege?
dinniman: Mongo! MONGO! (Mongo is wearing the hat. Mongo only says one sound at a time. Mongo votes twice. Mongo has never been happier.) Would you wear a silly hat, speak only one sound at a time and vote twice for the privilege?

plain: Would you happily communicate in single grunts if it doubled your vote?
dinniman: Ugh. Ug. Oog. Honestly, I've had worse conversations at bingo, and none of them came with two votes. Would you happily communicate in single grunts if it doubled your vote?

plain: Would you like the first four players to die to come straight back as Travellers?
dinniman: Died early? Bad luck! Here's a fresh backpack and a new career on the road, same team as before. Would you like the first four players to die to come straight back as Travellers?

plain: Do you believe the game's first few deaths should be a rebirth into a new travelling role rather than an ending?
dinniman: I've buried a lot of crawlers. Would've been nice if a few of them had just walked back in wearing a new coat. Do you believe the game's first few deaths should be a rebirth into a new travelling role rather than an ending?

plain: Would you like a game with two Storytellers, one who always lies and one who always tells the truth?
dinniman: Double the hosts, half the trust! One of them's lying to your face, and they might swap at dusk. Brand synergy! Would you like a game with two Storytellers, one who always lies and one who always tells the truth?

plain: Would you enjoy working out which of two Storytellers is the liar, knowing they might swap at dusk?
dinniman: One narrator lies, one tells the truth, and the guards hate you. Ask the right question or die stupid. Classic. Would you enjoy working out which of two Storytellers is the liar, knowing they might swap at dusk?

plain: As a rule-maker, would you allow any good character to appear more than once in the same game?
dinniman: Two of the same? Why not three? Beauty, my children, multiplies! I DECREE IT! As a rule-maker, would you allow any good character to appear more than once in the same game?

plain: Would you like a rule that means two players claiming the same good character, whichever it is, might both be honest?
dinniman: Two people say they are the same thing. Normally one is a liar. Under this rule? Maybe neither, for any good character at all. Good luck, everybody. Would you like a rule that means two players claiming the same good character, whichever it is, might both be honest?

plain: Would you shield one named good character from every death except execution, even though evil learns who they are?
dinniman: One player, wrapped in storm-proof bubble wrap! Only the gallows can get them! Downside: the bad guys get a big glowing arrow over their head! Would you shield one named good character from every death except execution, even though evil learns who they are?

plain: Would you like to announce before the game which good character the storm will spare from night-time deaths?
dinniman: Before the curtain rises, darling, you tell everyone exactly which hero the storm protects. Bold. Reckless. I adore it. Would you like to announce before the game which good character the storm will spare from night-time deaths?

plain: Would you like a game where nobody knows their own character or alignment until they die?
dinniman: No character sheet. No team colours. You find out who you were at your own funeral. The ratings will be ENORMOUS. Would you like a game where nobody knows their own character or alignment until they die?

plain: Would you play happily in the dark, learning who you really were only at the moment you die?
dinniman: Most of us don't know what we're doing down here anyway. At least this way it's official. Would you play happily in the dark, learning who you really were only at the moment you die?

plain: Would you reward a nominee who convincingly pretends to be a character nobody has claimed yet?
dinniman: A new face, a new voice, a whole new character pulled out of thin air in the dock. If the act is good enough, I'd let them live. Would you reward a nominee who convincingly pretends to be a character nobody has claimed yet?

plain: Do you love a performer who can throw their voice well enough to cheat the gallows?
dinniman: Gather round, folks! The dummy's talking, the nominee's sweating, and if the act lands they might walk away from the rope! Do you love a performer who can throw their voice well enough to cheat the gallows?

plain: Would you like to hand out secret goals that reward players with true information when achieved?
dinniman: Hidden quest assigned! Objective: classified! Reward: one genuine, certified, non-poisoned fact! Would you like to hand out secret goals that reward players with true information when achieved?

plain: Do you think players should earn information by completing a secret personal task rather than by using an ability?
dinniman: Sure, abilities are nice. But somebody hands me a weird little secret chore with a real answer as the prize? I am in. Every damn time. Do you think players should earn information by completing a secret personal task rather than by using an ability?

plain: As someone just passing through, would you like the power to kill a player with your own hand?
dinniman: You wander into town with a bedroll and a bad reputation, and you're allowed to end somebody personally. KILL! KILL! As someone just passing through, would you like the power to kill a player with your own hand?

plain: As a late arrival, would you like to wake at night and secretly pick a player to use your ability on?
dinniman: Everyone else is asleep. You're up, tiptoeing round the circle, choosing a target. Very creepy. Very effective. As a late arrival, would you like to wake at night and secretly pick a player to use your ability on?

plain: As a traveller, would you rather make your ability's choices during the day than at night?
dinniman: Some wanderers skulk about after dark. Others do their business in broad daylight with the whole town watching. Bold. Would get you killed on my floor. As a traveller, would you rather make your ability's choices during the day than at night?

plain: As a traveller, would you like to change who may nominate or vote for the entire town?
dinniman: New in town and already rewriting the constitution! The Founding Fathers would be appalled! The audience is THRILLED! As a traveller, would you like to change who may nominate or vote for the entire town?

plain: As a traveller, would you rather save a single big moment for the right time than act every day or night?
dinniman: Patience is a weapon. One shot, one moment, and you've got to pick it right. It's terrifying, but it's also kind of beautiful. As a traveller, would you rather save a single big moment for the right time than act every day or night?

plain: As a traveller, would you need a living player's agreement before your ability can work?
dinniman: Consent forms! Initial here, sign there, and only then do the fun things happen! Legal is so proud of you. As a traveller, would you need a living player's agreement before your ability can work?

plain: As a traveller, would you like your ability to teach you something private about another player?
dinniman: Oh, I'm not here for the scenery, darling. I'm here for the dirt. Who are they? Which side? Spill it. As a traveller, would you like your ability to teach you something private about another player?

plain: As a traveller, is your ability entirely about whether you yourself get removed from the game by the town?
dinniman: Some travellers have shiny powers. Some just have a very personal relationship with the noose. As a traveller, is your ability entirely about whether you yourself get removed from the game by the town?

plain: As a traveller, does your ability give, boost, restore or change someone's character or ability?
dinniman: Upgrade station now open! Grants! Buffs! Resurrections of skills! Unexpected transformations! Warranty void if used! As a traveller, does your ability give, boost, restore or change someone's character or ability?

plain: As a traveller, are you fussy about where people sit and how they conduct themselves?
dinniman: Elbows OFF the table. Sit where you are TOLD. No sneaking off for secret chats. Honestly, the manners in this dungeon. As a traveller, are you fussy about where people sit and how they conduct themselves?

plain: As a Fabled, are you mostly concerned with who may talk and when?
dinniman: Some helpers fix the numbers. Some fix the deaths. You fix the noise. As a Fabled, are you mostly concerned with who may talk and when?

plain: As a Fabled, are you mainly there to make the game kinder to new players?
dinniman: Everyone remembers their first time down here. It's awful. If your whole purpose is making that first game a little less awful, I think that's lovely. As a Fabled, are you mainly there to make the game kinder to new players?

plain: As a Fabled, would you hand players a new decision that any of them might get to make, which the normal rules don't offer?
dinniman: New interactive feature! Viewers, I mean players, now get a shiny extra button to press! What does it do? Press it and find out! As a Fabled, would you hand players a new decision that any of them might get to make, which the normal rules don't offer?

plain: As a Fabled, would you adjust how many Outsiders or evil players can end up in the game?
dinniman: Headcount management is a core brand value! Too many villains, too few misfits, it's all just numbers on a spreadsheet. As a Fabled, would you adjust how many Outsiders or evil players can end up in the game?

plain: As a Fabled, would you deliberately build a falsehood into the game that is never publicly corrected?
dinniman: One lie, darling, tucked in among the truths like a razor in a cake. And nobody will ever stand up and confess to it. As a Fabled, would you deliberately build a falsehood into the game that is never publicly corrected?

plain: As a Fabled, would you give the Demon a special decision that the normal rules don't allow?
dinniman: THE BEAST SHALL CHOOSE! It shall be granted powers beyond the rules! I, too, would like powers beyond the rules! As a Fabled, would you give the Demon a special decision that the normal rules don't allow?

plain: As a Fabled, is your effect about the Storyteller's own behaviour rather than the players'?
dinniman: Most rules keep the contestants in line. Yours keeps the guy behind the screen honest, or at least honestly bad at his job. As a Fabled, is your effect about the Storyteller's own behaviour rather than the players'?

plain: As a Fabled, is your influence aimed squarely at how the game ends?
dinniman: Forget the middle. Nobody remembers the middle. It's the FINALE that makes a star, darling. As a Fabled, is your influence aimed squarely at how the game ends?

plain: As a Fabled, do you keep players in line with the threat that something bad might happen to them?
dinniman: Something bad. Maybe. Could be nothing! Could be your head rolling across the floor! The suspense is DELICIOUS! As a Fabled, do you keep players in line with the threat that something bad might happen to them?

plain: As a hidden rule, do you only decide who receives which character, or how many copies of a character there are?
dinniman: Your work is done before anybody even opens their envelope. After that, you just sit back and watch the chaos you planted. As a hidden rule, do you only decide who receives which character, or how many copies of a character there are?

plain: As a rule-bender, do you change how nominees get to defend themselves?
dinniman: Welcome to the trial segment! Our nominees have a brand-new way to plead for their lives tonight, and the audience is ready to judge! As a rule-bender, do you change how nominees get to defend themselves?

plain: As a hidden rule, would you restrict how players are allowed to speak?
dinniman: Mongo... hm. (Mongo is very quiet now. Mongo has learned that some rules decide who can talk and how much, and Mongo does not want trouble.) As a hidden rule, would you restrict how players are allowed to speak?

plain: As a hidden rule, do you change what happens to a player at the moment they die?
dinniman: Death down here usually just means a loot box and a sad little ghost. Your rule makes it mean something else. As a hidden rule, do you change what happens to a player at the moment they die?

plain: As a rule-bender, would you reward players for putting on a performance?
dinniman: Grunt like a caveman, act like someone you're not, and the game gives you a prize. I've seen worse game design. Not much worse. As a rule-bender, would you reward players for putting on a performance?

plain: Behind the Storyteller's screen, would you change how many Outsiders or evil players there can be?
dinniman: Population control, but make it fun! A misfit added here, a villain capped there. Spreadsheets are the real final boss! Behind the Storyteller's screen, would you change how many Outsiders or evil players there can be?

plain: Behind the screen, would you have the Storyteller openly get things wrong or tell lies?
dinniman: The person running this whole show, standing up and lying, or fumbling it in public. Now THAT is television. Behind the screen, would you have the Storyteller openly get things wrong or tell lies?

plain: As a rule-bender behind the Storyteller, would you control when or how players are allowed to talk?
dinniman: Who speaks, when they speak, how many sounds they're allowed to make. Honestly, some of these rules are just a very elaborate 'shut up'. As a rule-bender behind the Storyteller, would you control when or how players are allowed to talk?

plain: Behind the screen, would you change who may vote or how many votes somebody gets?
dinniman: Voting reform! Very serious! Very civic! Some ghosts get a ballot, some guy in a hat gets two! Behind the screen, would you change who may vote or how many votes somebody gets?

plain: Behind the screen, is all your work done before the first night, deciding who gets which character or how many of a kind are dealt?
dinniman: Some of us meddle all game. You do your mischief at the dealing table and then put your feet up. Respect. Behind the screen, is all your work done before the first night, deciding who gets which character or how many of a kind are dealt?

plain: Behind the screen, would you hand some players extra secret information about the game in progress?
dinniman: Free intel! Bonus scrolls! Exclusive spoilers for selected contestants! Terms and conditions apply! Behind the screen, would you hand some players extra secret information about the game in progress?

plain: Of the two vote-meddlers, would you rather inflate someone's vote than turn it against them?
dinniman: Both of you mess with ballots overnight, fine. But one of you adds and one of you subtracts. Which kind of crook are you? Of the two vote-meddlers, would you rather inflate someone's vote than turn it against them?

plain: Would you rather your boost come round every night than be a single favour for the whole game?
dinniman: Loyalty card or one golden ticket, darling? One of these brings coffee every single night. The other brings one spooky miracle and then closes up shop. Would you rather your boost come round every night than be a single favour for the whole game?

plain: Of these daytime killers, would you rather kill to protect a teammate than to settle a score?
dinniman: Some killers shoot voters. Some do favours for neighbours. And some only strike when someone comes after their buddy. Of these daytime killers, would you rather kill to protect a teammate than to settle a score?

plain: Of these daytime killers, would you only strike once the person beside you has given the go-ahead?
dinniman: Proper organised crime runs on handshakes and favours! Very traditional! Excellent for brand loyalty! Of these daytime killers, would you only strike once the person beside you has given the go-ahead?

plain: Of these two execution-forcers, would you want the power to spare the accused as well as condemn them?
dinniman: One of you can only ever say 'hang them'. The other gets to say 'let them go', too. Mercy is a choice, and it's the harder one. Of these two execution-forcers, would you want the power to spare the accused as well as condemn them?

plain: Would you rather wait until the final day to give the dead their voice back?
dinniman: Ghosts voting all game long, or one grand ghostly return for the season finale? Ratings say finale. Always finale. Would you rather wait until the final day to give the dead their voice back?

plain: Of the silence-keepers, would you single out experienced players to keep quiet?
dinniman: Not everybody shuts up. Just the know-it-alls with fifty games under their belts. I like it already. Of the silence-keepers, would you single out experienced players to keep quiet?

plain: Of the silence-keepers, would you let exactly one chosen person speak while everyone else waits?
dinniman: One speaker. One spotlight. Everybody else waits their turn like civilised people. I have NEVER understood why this isn't how every conversation works. Of the silence-keepers, would you let exactly one chosen person speak while everyone else waits?

plain: As a protector of newcomers, would you rather punish whoever harms them than give them room to speak?
dinniman: There's a gentle way to look after beginners and a SMITING way. I strongly recommend the smiting way. As a protector of newcomers, would you rather punish whoever harms them than give them room to speak?

plain: Of these two who ask permission, would you ask in order to learn something rather than to kill?
dinniman: You both need a yes from somebody. One of you wants a secret. The other wants a body. Do you want the secret? Of these two who ask permission, would you ask in order to learn something rather than to kill?

plain: Of these two curious travellers, would you rather learn someone's exact character than just their alignment?
dinniman: Good or evil is the boring headline, darling. I want the full biography, the real name, the dirty laundry. Of these two curious travellers, would you rather learn someone's exact character than just their alignment?

plain: Of these two rule-rewriting travellers, would you rather control nominations than votes?
dinniman: Pick your poison: decide who ends up in the dock, or decide who gets to raise a hand. THE ACCUSATION IS EVERYTHING! Of these two rule-rewriting travellers, would you rather control nominations than votes?

plain: Of these two, would you rather protect yourself from removal than risk dying in someone else's place?
dinniman: One of these guys cracks jokes to stay alive. The other volunteers to hang for his friends. I know which one I'd rather have a beer with, but that's not the question. Of these two, would you rather protect yourself from removal than risk dying in someone else's place?

plain: Of the character-changers, would you set off a transformation without having to die first?
dinniman: Some transformations only trigger off your corpse. Others you can fire off whenever, while still breathing. Breathing is good. Of the character-changers, would you set off a transformation without having to die first?

plain: Of the character-changers, would you like the Storyteller, not you or your team, to decide exactly who transforms?
dinniman: You pull the lever. The Storyteller decides whose face melts. That's not your problem, that's management's problem. Of the character-changers, would you like the Storyteller, not you or your team, to decide exactly who transforms?

plain: Would you rather the whole table be ignorant of their own characters, not just you?
dinniman: If I've got to stumble around not knowing what I am, so does everyone else. Fair's fair. Would you rather the whole table be ignorant of their own characters, not just you?

plain: Would you rather the Storyteller's slip-ups be owned up to than be deliberate, ongoing lies?
dinniman: A public apology is a PR opportunity! A lying narrator is a lawsuit! Both are content, but one of them tests better. Would you rather the Storyteller's slip-ups be owned up to than be deliberate, ongoing lies?

plain: Of these three sources of false information, would you have the lie land on someone who has come to visit you?
dinniman: You invited them in. You poured the tea. And one of them leaves with a lie in their pocket. Of these three sources of false information, would you have the lie land on someone who has come to visit you?

plain: Of these three sources of false information, would you have the falsehood be about how a player registers?
dinniman: Not a lie told to anyone, exactly. Just a player who shows up wrong, once, on somebody's reading. Sneaky. Of these three sources of false information, would you have the falsehood be about how a player registers?

plain: Would you allow duplicates of any good character, rather than just one particular character?
dinniman: Twins, triplets, a whole choir of identical heroes, and not just one kind! MORE! MORE OF EVERYTHING! Would you allow duplicates of any good character, rather than just one particular character?

plain: Of these two, would you bring the dead back as a different kind of character from what they were?
dinniman: Resurrection is boring if they come back exactly the same. New hat, new name, new career on the road. Of these two, would you bring the dead back as a different kind of character from what they were?

plain: Would you rather assign every player's character than just decide who the Minions are?
dinniman: Picking your henchmen is fine. Picking EVERYONE is art. I would hand-place every single one of my fans. Would you rather assign every player's character than just decide who the Minions are?

plain: Of these two double-nominators, would you only want your extra nomination after an execution has already happened?
dinniman: One of you gets two nominations after dying. The other waits for the first hanging to finish, then calls for an encore. Of these two double-nominators, would you only want your extra nomination after an execution has already happened?

plain: Of these two truth-benders, would you rather players earn true information than gamble on which narrator to trust?
dinniman: Mongo work hard! Mongo get prize! (Mongo would much rather complete a task and get a real answer than guess which of two shifty humans is lying.) Of these two truth-benders, would you rather players earn true information than gamble on which narrator to trust?
